ORDER This criminal appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 has been filed assailing the order dated 16.12.2022, passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989, District Khandwa (M.P.), whereby first bail application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the applicant has been dismissed.
Appellant has been arrested in connection with the Crime No.472/2022 of P.S.Mandhata, District Khandwa (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 294, 323, 376, 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC and Section 3-1(w)(ii), 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story on 25.11.2022, 27 year old prosecutrix along with her former husband appeared at police station and lodged FIR stating that she is a labourer.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: About 4-5 months ago, she came in contact with Krishna.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: They developed intimacy.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: One day Krishna took her in hotel Deepak in Onkareshwar and established physical relations.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, he established physical relations with her for number of occasions.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Krishna is already married.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Today at around 03:00 p.m. Krishna refused to marry with her and abused and beat her.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: FIR was registered.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant has not committed any offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: He is innocent.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: He has been falsely implicated.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: In this case, appellant and prosecutrix both are major and married.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: They were having consensual sexual relationship.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Appellant never established any physical relations with the prosecutrix on promise of marriage.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: False FIR has been registered as appellant did not succumb to the illegal demands made by the prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore, it has been prayed that appellant be released on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Government Advocate has opposed the grant of bail to the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre trial detention of the appellant is not warranted.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Consequently, appeal stands allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: I t is directed that appellant - Krishna be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Krishna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.

opennyai_summary.20_February_2023__facts:
ORDER This criminal appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 has been filed assailing the order dated 16.12.2022, passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989, District Khandwa (M.P.), whereby first bail application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the applicant has been dismissed.
Appellant has been arrested in connection with the Crime No.472/2022 of P.S.Mandhata, District Khandwa (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 294, 323, 376, 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC and Section 3-1(w)(ii), 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989.
opennyai_summary.20_February_2023__arguments:
In this case, appellant and prosecutrix both are major and married.
They were having consensual sexual relationship.
Appellant never established any physical relations with the prosecutrix on promise of marriage.
False FIR has been registered as appellant did not succumb to the illegal demands made by the prosecutrix.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the other hand, learned Government Advocate has opposed the grant of bail to the appellant.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre trial detention of the appellant is not warranted.
opennyai_summary.20_February_2023__decision:
Consequently, appeal stands allowed.
I t is directed that appellant - Krishna be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

Author: Subodh Abhyankar
Bench: Subodh Abhyankar
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:29205
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Subodh Abhyankar
 On The 7 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 43797 of 2025
 Krishna
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Manish Yadav - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Vishal Singh Panwar - G.A. for State.
Order 
1] They are heard and perused the case diary.
2] This is the applicant's second bail application filed under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/ Section 439 of Cr.P.C. as he is implicated in connection with Crime No.161/2023 registered at Police Station Udainagar, District- Dewas (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376 & 376(2)(N) of IPC and Sections 5L/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 24.12.2023.
opennyai_summary.final__facts:
His first application M.Cr.C. No.44264 of 2024 was dismissed by this Court on 05.11.2024 on merits.
3] The allegation against the applicant is of abduction and rape.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
4] Counsel has submitted that although his earlier application has already been dismissed, but the prosecutrix has already been examined, and there are material omissions and contradictions in her statement, and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29205 2 MCRC-43797-2025 admittedly, she has resided with the applicant for around 7 months, and her age is also disputed, and the applicant is lodged in jail since 24.12.2023.
Thus, it is prayed that the application be allowed.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
6] Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case-diary and taking note of the period of incarceration, and the fact that the prosecutrix has also resided with the applicant for around 7 months, her age is also disputed, this Court is inclined to allow the present application.
7] Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is hereby allowed.
The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
8] Accordingly, the application is allowed and disposed of.
